analyst_view.overall: Lille are 35th with 1 point from 4 games, so this is close to their last chance to reach the play-offs, though they sit 2nd in Ligue 1 under Davide Ancelotti. Bayern (13th, 8 points) arrive badly hit: Harry Kane tore an ankle ligament against Köln on Friday, had surgery and is out for about three months, and Michael Olise left that game on crutches (the club calls it precaution). Serge Gnabry, Ismael Saibari, Alphonso Davies and Manuel Neuer were already out and Luis Díaz is only slowly returning. The numbers list nobody missing, so Kane's absence is not in them; that is the main reason my view drops Bayern's attack. No referee is named yet.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals, 1.9 of them Bayern's, and do not know that Kane is out. Kane is Bayern's main scorer, and with Olise doubtful and Gnabry and Saibari also out, Bayern's attack is much thinner; Lille needing a win keeps their own side up. Two sources confirm the Kane injury, so I take about 12% off, to about 2.7.

corners.text: The numbers expect 9.4 corners, split almost evenly. Bayern without Kane may attack less directly but still dominate the ball, while Lille must push for a win at home; these pull in opposite directions, so I stay at 9.4.

cards.text: The numbers expect 3.4 cards and already take about 11% off Bayern for their low recent card count. The referee is not named yet. Lille's must-win mood could add a booking late on, but that is a hunch, so I stay at 3.4.

shots.text: The numbers say 25 shots, nearly 15 from Bayern. Bayern still create a lot without Kane, but losing him and maybe Olise, their two most frequent shooters, should cut their total somewhat; Lille needing a win stops me going further. About 24.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.9 shots on target. Kane puts a high share of his shots on target, and without him (and possibly Olise) Bayern's accuracy should drop more than their volume, which the numbers can't see. I go down to about 8.3.
